walkthroughs.body_html:
A tropical storm is a giant low-pressure system with:

• Winds over 119 km/h
• Torrential rain
• Storm surges
• A spinning structure

Same storm — different names by region!

The same type of storm has different names:

• Hurricane — Atlantic / NE Pacific
• Typhoon — NW Pacific (Japan, Philippines)
• Cyclone — Indian Ocean, Australia

Wind speed and structure are identical.

Tropical storms have three key parts:

1. Eye — calm, clear centre (~30 km wide)
2. Eyewall — strongest winds, heaviest rain
3. Rain bands — spiral arms of cloud

The eyewall is the most dangerous part.
